scenarios.title: Parallel Feature Branches Merge
scenarios.description: Two feature branches modify the same function independently
scenarios.example_conflict:
<<<<<<< HEAD
def calculate_total(items):
    total = sum(item.price for item in items)
    tax = total * 0.08
    return total + tax
=======
def calculate_total(items):
    subtotal = sum(item.price * item.quantity for item in items)
    return subtotal
>>>>>>> feature/cart-updates
step_by_step: 1. Analyze both implementations to understand intent
2. Determine if both features are needed
alternative_approaches: Create separate functions for each feature
Use feature flags to toggle behaviors
Refactor into a more flexible design
common_pitfalls: Blindly accepting one side without analysis
prevention_tips: Use better code organization to minimize conflicts

best_practices.title: Keep Feature Branches Short-Lived
best_practices.description: Minimize conflicts by merging feature branches frequently
implementation: Limit feature branch lifetime to 2-3 days
Break large features into smaller incremental changes
examples: Instead of one large feature branch, create multiple smaller PRs
Use feature flags to merge incomplete features safely
anti_patterns: Waiting until feature is 'perfect' before merging

best_practices.title: Regularly Sync with Main Branch
best_practices.description: Keep feature branches up-to-date with main to reduce conflict size
implementation: Rebase or merge main into feature branch daily
Stay aware of changes in main branch
anti_patterns: Never syncing until ready to merge

best_practices.title: Use Automated Code Formatters
best_practices.description: Eliminate formatting conflicts with consistent automated formatting
implementation: Use tools like Black, Prettier, gofmt
examples: pre-commit hook with black for Python

best_practices.title: Enable Git Rerere
best_practices.description: Let Git remember how you resolved conflicts previously
examples: Rerere automatically resolves repeated conflicts during rebases
anti_patterns: Not using rerere for repetitive conflicts
Resolving same conflict multiple times manually

best_practices.title: Test After Every Conflict Resolution
best_practices.description: Always verify that resolved conflicts don't break functionality
implementation: Run full test suite after resolution
examples: npm test or pytest after resolving conflicts
anti_patterns: Assuming resolution is correct without verification

best_practices.title: Communicate During Conflict Resolution
best_practices.description: Coordinate with team members when resolving complex conflicts
implementation: Discuss resolution approach in team chat
Document resolution rationale in commit message
examples: Tag teammate in PR comment: 'Hey @author, which approach should we use?'
Detailed commit message explaining why certain approach was chosen
anti_patterns: Silently resolving conflicts without consulting others

best_practices.title: Learn from Conflicts
best_practices.description: Analyze patterns in conflicts to prevent future occurrences
implementation: Track which files conflict most often
examples: If config file always conflicts, split into multiple files
If function conflicts frequently, it may be doing too much
anti_patterns: Treating conflicts as normal without analysis
Not learning from repeated conflict patterns
